label: Build and PROVE an end-to-end decoder: ./transmitter <payload> out.wav -> demod

objective: Build and PROVE an end-to-end decoder: ./transmitter <payload> out.wav -> demod -> symbols -> recovered payload, using known-plaintext/differential experiments with the local transmitter binary.
detail:
Workspace: C:/Users/Duhamster/Prog/insomnia/inslopnia_harness/ctf-runs/chik-chirik/workspace (a WSL/bash-friendly env; transmitter is a Linux ELF - run it via WSL bash if needed). Prior round artifacts already here: demod.py (4-level chirp demod, 2048 samples/symbol, quantizes total freq delta to +-1000/+-2000 Hz), symdump.py, chirp_seg.py, analyze_wav.py, probe_positions.py (statistical known-plaintext probe), s_*.npy (demodulated symbol streams), probe_*.npy, len_*.wav / p*.wav / m*.wav / r*.wav / rnd*.wav (prior transmitter runs), tx_model.py / enc_model.py / rev_model.py (reversed models, partially guesswork). DO NOT restart from scratch - verify and extend.

Goal: a decoder that recovers the payload from the symbol stream WITHOUT knowing the PRNG seed (seed comes from /dev/urandom per run). Method:
1. Sanity: run ./transmitter with a known payload several times, demod each run; check symbol count is stable and equals the expected count from tx_model.py (ngroups = ceil? bits/3, 7 symbols per group - VERIFY this). Determine which symbol positions are constant across runs with the same payload (data-dependent) vs random (PRNG bits).
2. Differential mapping: payloads differing in exactly one bit -> find which symbol positions/levels change -> derive the exact symbol-position -> payload-bit mapping and level -> value mapping. Watch out: demod.py's level labels (0..3) may be permuted vs the transmitter's byte values; the parity byte may also depend on data (running parity) - account for cascading parity effects.
3. Check whether more than 2 bits per symbol are modulated (e.g. start frequency, amplitude) - use symdump.py output on known runs; if the data-carrying positions show >4 distinct states, extend the demod.
4. Also verify symbol boundary alignment (no preamble/offset in capture.wav vs transmitter output - compare structure of s_cap.npy with your own runs).
5. Write decoder as decode_sym.py (input: wav path or .npy symbol stream; output: recovered payload bytes) plus a self-test mode: generate >=5 random payloads of various lengths 8..64, run ./transmitter, demod, decode, assert equality; exit 0 on success, nonzero otherwise. Also write WORKLOG_A.md summarizing the established facts (positions, mapping, parity, any corrections to tx_model.py).
Leave all artifacts in the workspace. Do not modify demod.py's interface destructively - copy/extend if needed.

label: From the existing disassembly (modfn.asm, tx.asm, disasm.txt) nail down the EXAC

objective: From the existing disassembly (modfn.asm, tx.asm, disasm.txt) nail down the EXACT per-group output byte composition (which bits are PRNG, which carry data, parity semantics) and the symbol->chirp-level mapping; assess whether the payload is recoverable without the PRNG seed.
detail:
Workspace: C:/Users/Duhamster/Prog/insomnia/inslopnia_harness/ctf-runs/chik-chirik/workspace. Read-only-ish analysis step: produce rev_notes.md; do NOT edit demod.py, decode_sym.py or tx_model.py (another agent works on those). You may run ./transmitter and your own throwaway scripts (prefix filenames with b_) for spot checks.

Context: prior round reversed the Jai binary 'transmitter' (non-PIE ELF, .text 0x209ab0..0x258a38). Key functions: encode entry 0x21ed90, WHITEN 0x220750, prng step 0x210f80 (4xu32 state, returns 1 parity bit: parity32(x[3]&0xa361c95b) ^ parity32(x[1]&0x7d284e13)), parity helper 0x20b9b0, rotl 0x20bc90, tables at 0x201170/0x201178/0x201180. Existing guesses in tx_model.py/enc_model.py are PARTIALLY WRONG (e.g. out[i]=(r0<<2)|(r1<<1)|p exceeds 3 but chirp seems 4-level; the '(c0<<4)|(c1<<2)|(c2)' byte is a guess).

Deliverables in rev_notes.md:
1. Exact structure of the 7 output bytes per 3-bit group: for each byte, which bits come from PRNG stream, which from data bits c0..c2, which from running parity; the exact parity update equation; order of prng.next() calls.
2. The exact mapping output-byte-value -> chirp parameters (slope/level, maybe start freq): read table 0x201180 ([2,0,3,1]?) and the modulation code (modfn.asm around the symbol loop; encoder writes 2048 samples per symbol with env window and phase = t*symbol_rate + dither). Determine how many distinct symbol values exist (4? 8?) and what physical parameter each maps to.
3. Verdict: is the payload recoverable from the symbol stream without the PRNG seed (i.e. do data bits appear in clear or only via parity)? If only via parity XOR PRNG, say so explicitly and describe what constraints are known (this changes the whole attack).
4. Corrected encode() pseudocode precise enough to implement.
Cross-check each conclusion with at least one spot experiment (e.g. patch nothing; run ./transmitter with crafted payloads and compare demod output via existing demod.py imported read-only).

label: Run a FRESH known-payload roundtrip of the real ./transmitter binary through the

objective: Run a FRESH known-payload roundtrip of the real ./transmitter binary through the full decode chain, then decode capture.wav and extract the ctfcup{...} flag.
detail:
Workspace: C:/Users/Duhamster/Prog/insomnia/inslopnia_harness/ctf-runs/chik-chirik/workspace. NOTE: the asm-verify agent was watchdog-killed after persisting its artifacts (exact_model.py, verify_model.py) - they are on disk and are the ground-truth reversed model, but its final roundtrip run was NOT observed; treat the roundtrip as unproven until you run it. Another agent (empirical-decoder) may still be running; coordinate by files, do not overwrite its outputs (WORKLOG_A.md, decode_sym.py), use your own filenames.

The encoding is fully modeled in exact_model.py (whiten: out=(r0<<2)|(r1<<1)|p, p=prev^d^r2, MSB-first bits of payload++u32le(len); RS(7,3) over GF(8) poly 0xB, codeword=P(1..7); 8 preamble symbols [0,3,4,7,7,4,3,0]; 8-level chirps: 4 endpoints 4000/5000/7000/8000 Hz from center 6000, 2048 samp @48kHz, polarity = s&1). verify_model.py contains a working 8-level demodulator (template correlation) and the full blind-decode chain including the GF(2) solve for the 128-bit RNG state from the r0/r1 leak.

MANDATORY ORDER (operator directive):
1. FIRST run a FRESH end-to-end roundtrip on the real binary: python verify_model.py --fresh 2>&1 | tee verify_roundtrip.log. It must print ALL CHECKS PASSED (transmit -> demod8 -> preamble -> RS decode -> GF(2) solve -> blind decode == payload). Do not proceed to capture.wav until this passes; if it fails, debug/fix the chain (compare intermediate stages against a shimmed-seed run using randshim.so if needed) and re-run.
2. Then decode capture.wav: demod8 -> verify preamble [0,3,4,7,7,4,3,0] (symbol count: nsym = 8 + 7*ngroups; derive payload length n from ngroups, cross-check with the u32le trailer; if the preamble is not at position 0, search for it; RS(7,3) corrects up to 2 symbol errors per group - report per-group error counts) -> RS decode -> GF(2) solve using ALL r0/r1 equations (check consistency/nullspace; optionally constrain with known trailer bits and flag prefix 'ctfcup{') -> unwhiten -> payload bytes.
3. Validate: payload printable ASCII, starts with ctfcup{ and ends with }, trailer u32le == len(payload). If multiple solutions (nullspace), enumerate candidates and check the format.
4. Write the exact flag to FLAG.txt (newline-terminated) and the full decode transcript to WORKLOG_FINAL.md (commands, outputs, per-group RS error stats, solved RNG state hex).
Report the exact flag in your final summary.
